new_terms.definition: The script that LSF starts on the worker server for one job of Distributed Dice. It starts the command of the job there.
The host mode in which one Dice daemon serves all users of the server. The file `/etc/positron/dice.yaml` selects it with `mode: shared`.
The script that submits a build command to an LSF worker. The remote job starts with an empty environment. The script passes on a fixed list of variables.
The installer of Rust toolchains. `rust/rust-toolchain.sh` runs it outside the Nix dev shell.

A third-party command-line tool from Google that reads and writes hardware registers (PCI, memory-mapped I/O, I/O ports, CPU model-specific registers). A copy is in `bin/iotools-1.5`. No TRON build file builds it.
The Linux driver that gives a user program direct access to a PCI device, such as an FPGA card.
The two Perfetto daemons. `traced` is the tracing service. `traced_probes` collects kernel events.
The two launcher scripts for Perfetto traces. They start the Perfetto programs. Both load `perfetto/launcher-common`.
The compiler tool that reports data races at run time. `make test-tsan` runs the test programs in `gen-tsan` that are built with it.
The file that `rust/rust-toolchain.sh` writes. `rust/run-cargo` reads it outside Nix to find the Rust installation.
The Python package tool. `bin/ci/check-lock-freshness.sh` runs `uv lock --check` on the `uv.lock` files of the repository.
The development environment that `nix develop .#lint` starts. It holds the pinned lint tools.
The pytest suites under `t/proxy`. They send requests to a rinzler_proxy process on `127.0.0.1`.
A set of PCI devices that the Linux kernel isolates together. `/dev/vfio/<number>` is the device file of one group.
The compiler cache that the `make` and CMake builds use. `CCACHE_DIR` names its directory.
One build recipe of Nix. The files under `nix/` and `flake.nix` define the derivations of the repository.
A test that `flake.nix` defines under `checks`. `nix flake check` or `nix build .#checks.<system>.<name>` runs it.
The HTTP client module of the Python standard library. `bin/slice`, `bin/hugepage_exhaustion_repro.py` and `bin/ci/hf_cache.py` send their requests with it.
A third-party Python HTTP client library. `t/proxy/tools/capture.py` and the replay tests send their requests with it.
The user account list of the operating system, for example `/etc/passwd`. Python reads it with `pwd.getpwuid`.

notes: No row is dropped. All 24 rows were checked against the checkout at commit 7eddde7895. All evidence quotes of the input matched their source lines. Facts that are not in the checkout carry the version in the cell. They were tested or read outside the checkout: Python 3.10.12 (`urllib.request.getproxies_environment`, `proxy_bypass_environment`, `getpass.getuser`, `tempfile`), GNU coreutils 8.32 (`mktemp`), g++ 11.4.0 (`std::filesystem::temp_directory_path`), CMake 3.22.1 (`$env{USER}` in a preset), GNU Make (`?=` with `$(USER)`), and httpx 0.28.1 (`get_environment_proxies`, read from the wheel whose SHA-256 is listed in `t/proxy/uv.lock`, the lock file of the `t/proxy` tools). `tron_use` counts test code as TRON code. changes.now: Python `urllib` inside `bin/slice` and `bin/ci/hf_cache.py`. The httpx library inside `t/proxy/tools/capture.py`, for an `https` value of `--base-url`. No TRON file reads the name itself. `t/proxy/test_rzproxy.py` sets it.

changes.name: https_proxy
changes.was: `bin/slice` downloads only when `TIKTOKEN_ENCODINGS_BASE` is unset and the cached file is missing or has a wrong hash. `urllib` prefers this lower-case name over `HTTPS_PROXY` (rule of Python 3.10.12). `t/proxy/README.md` states that `t/proxy/tools/capture.py` also honors the proxy variables.
changes.now: `bin/slice` downloads only when `TIKTOKEN_ENCODINGS_BASE` is unset and the cached file is missing or has a wrong hash. `urllib` prefers this lower-case name over `HTTPS_PROXY` (Python 3.10.12). Other tools, for example `curl`, `nix` and the Hugging Face library in `bin/get_model`, apply their own proxy rules.
changes.why: The row named only 2 Python tools. Model downloads go through another library: `snapshot_download` of huggingface_hub at bin/get_model:9 and :22. The row now says that such tools apply their own rules. The capture.py sentence moved to read_by.

changes.name: no_proxy
changes.was: Python `urllib` inside `bin/slice`, `bin/hugepage_exhaustion_repro.py` and `bin/ci/hf_cache.py`. No TRON file reads the name itself. Two test files set it.
changes.now: Python `urllib` inside `bin/slice`, `bin/hugepage_exhaustion_repro.py` and `bin/ci/hf_cache.py`. The httpx library inside `t/proxy/tools/capture.py`. No TRON file reads the name itself. Two test files set it.
changes.why: The cell left out the httpx reader. The comment at t/proxy/test_rzproxy.py:3693-3694 says that httpx reads `NO_PROXY` through `getproxies` of `urllib`. httpx 0.28.1 source, read outside the checkout from the wheel whose SHA-256 is in t/proxy/uv.lock:260: `get_environment_proxies` in httpx/_utils.py calls `urllib.request.getproxies()` and uses the keys `http`, `https`, `all` and `no`.

changes.name: no_proxy
changes.was: Host names or domain suffixes, separated by commas. `*` means every host. This is the rule of Python `urllib`.
changes.now: Host names, addresses or domain suffixes, separated by commas. The single text `*` means every host. This is the rule of Python `urllib`.
changes.why: `*` is special in `urllib` only when it is the whole value (`proxy_bypass_environment`, Python 3.10.12, tested outside the checkout). The tests set an address, not a host name: bin/slice-tests/test_integration.py:1493.

changes.name: no_proxy
changes.was: The read happens inside `urllib`, not in TRON code. The rules are those of Python 3.10.12. The fixture `loopback_only` in `bin/slice-tests/test_integration.py` sets `127.0.0.1`. A test in `t/proxy/test_rzproxy.py` sets an empty value.
changes.now: `urllib` reads the variable, not TRON code. The rules are those of Python 3.10.12. httpx 0.28.1 applies its own matching rules to the same list. The fixture `loopback_only` in `bin/slice-tests/test_integration.py` sets `127.0.0.1`. A test in `t/proxy/test_rzproxy.py` sets an empty value.
changes.why: Adds that httpx does its own matching. httpx 0.28.1 source, read outside the checkout from the wheel whose SHA-256 is in t/proxy/uv.lock:260: `get_environment_proxies` in httpx/_utils.py calls `urllib.request.getproxies()` and uses the keys `http`, `https`, `all` and `no`. For example, httpx treats `*` as 'no proxy at all' when it is any one entry of the list.

changes.name: http_proxy
changes.was: Unset: `urllib` uses `HTTP_PROXY` when that is set. Otherwise the tools connect directly. Empty: `urllib` uses no proxy, also when `HTTP_PROXY` is set.
changes.now: Unset: `urllib` uses `HTTP_PROXY` when that is set. Otherwise it connects directly. Empty: `urllib` uses no proxy, also when `HTTP_PROXY` is set.
changes.why: 'The tools connect directly' was too broad. httpx in t/proxy/tools/capture.py:39 can still use an `all_proxy` value. The cell now speaks only of `urllib` (bin/hugepage_exhaustion_repro.py:94), tested with Python 3.10.12 outside the checkout.

changes.why: 'The tools connect directly' was too broad, for the same reason as in the row `http_proxy`. The cell now speaks only of `urllib` (bin/slice:1823, bin/ci/hf_cache.py:355), tested with Python 3.10.12 outside the checkout.

changes.name: TSAN_OPTIONS
changes.was: `make test-tsan` runs 8 test programs that are built with ThreadSanitizer. It sets this value on each command. The value names the suppression file of the repository.
changes.now: `make test-tsan` runs 8 test programs that are built with ThreadSanitizer. It sets this value on each command. The value names `t/tsan/suppressions.txt`, the list of reports that ThreadSanitizer ignores.
changes.why: 'The suppression file of the repository' did not say what the file does. t/tsan/README.md:3-7 says that the suppression files filter false positives. t/tsan/suppressions.txt:8-9 gives the rule for an entry.
